close_reason: Won't fix: opinion-tagged. .expect() in test-helper construction is the standard idiom; failure shows up as a panic with a clear message identifying the helper. Refactoring to Result<_, _> would force every integration test to add ? plumbing. Section-3 paper-cut, defer.
description:
tests/helpers.rs:53-59:
```
let client = jmap_base_client::JmapClient::new(...)
    .expect("make_client: JmapClient construction must succeed");
```

This is a test helper, so `.expect` is acceptable in principle (review-rusty rules: 'unwrap/expect outside of tests, examples, or provably unreachable paths'). And tests are tests.

But the helper is used by every integration test — if construction ever fails (CA bundle problem on a CI machine, port already bound, etc.), the panic shows up in EVERY test name with a stack trace pointing at helpers.rs, not the test that called it. Returning Result and using `?` in callers (or letting the test framework render the failure) gives better localized output.

Lower priority — pure test ergonomics. Filing because it's a pattern that scales poorly.
title: make_client uses .expect() — should propagate as test failure
